$comment: Machine-readable record of every field test: a build in a hand, on a real device, against the live relay. This exists because the defects that reach this stage are the ones no test and no CI run can see — a ViewModel recreated by Android, a location provider that answers fast and coarse, an EXIF block that is simply absent. Each entry is what was OBSERVED, kept separate from what was CONCLUDED: `timeline` and `report` are transcribed from client_events and D1 and must never be edited to fit a later understanding, while `findings` is interpretation and may be revised. Written after the fact from the relay's own records, so a test that produced nothing to read produces no entry. The `docs/research/` write-up of a test cites the id here; a decision that a test caused cites it too.
source: D1 tables client_events and reports on the live relay, plus Cloudflare Workers Logs
notes: Timelines are transcribed verbatim, including the events that record a mistake. A tester who changed their mind produced two category-chosen events; both stay. Trimming a timeline to the happy path destroys the only evidence of what the interaction actually felt like.

atMs is milliseconds since the telemetry session began, which is the app process starting. It is the only ordering that survives: the relay stamps received_at at flush time, so every event in one batch shares it and the batch boundaries are invisible in that column.
A session id is random per process, never persisted, and cannot follow anyone between sessions (data/relay-events.json). Recording it here links a timeline to its report and to nothing else.
dryRun records whether the relay was armed. A test against an unarmed relay proves the app and the relay and says nothing about the city.

tests.what: First run of the Android app on real hardware against the live relay: the whole walk from camera to a recorded report, twice, by the developer indoors.

device.note: The developer's own phone, sideloaded over adb. Not a tester device.

build.signingNote: Android has no release signing chain yet (#58); the parity manifest records signed-release as ios-only. A release VARIANT was required regardless, because the relay host is a buildConfigField and only the release variant carries the deployed one.
build.hostVerifiedOn: the artifact, not the build log: the deployed host is present in classes.dex and no loopback literal is

relay.note: Unarmed throughout. Nothing in this test could reach the city, which is why it was safe to run and why it says nothing about the city's behaviour.

report.municipalityCheck: passed; the coordinate reverse-looked to SVFNR 0000, Reykjavíkurborg
report.descriptionShape: the typed text, then a blank line, then the relay's appended nearest registered address

server.note: No exception, no warning, no rejection anywhere in Workers Logs for the window.

confirmed.claim: A photo the app captures itself carries no EXIF GPS, so the device fix is the primary source on the capture path rather than the fallback.
confirmed.evidence: location-failed {reason: no-exif} preceded the device fix on both captures, at elapsedMs 1 and 0.
confirmed.wherePredicted: AGENTS.md, from CameraX's documented behaviour; docs/research/photos-exif-and-formats.md
confirmed.note: First observation of this on real Android hardware. It had been reasoned about, not measured.

confirmed.claim: The whole chain works end to end from a phone: camera, coordinate, category, relay, D1.
confirmed.evidence: send-result 201 in 1390 ms, and a matching row in reports.

confirmed.claim: A 2.29 MB JPEG passes the relay's size and magic-byte gates.
confirmed.evidence: photoBytes 2290923 recorded, no rejection. The city's stated limit is 8 MB.

findings.what: app-opened fired twice in one session, 16 minutes apart, because it was emitted from PocViewModel's init and a ViewModel is Activity-scoped while the telemetry session is process-scoped.
findings.evidence: atMs 1 and atMs 955703, same session id, therefore the same process.
findings.whyOnlyHere: No unit test can observe an Activity being recreated, and CI cannot background an app. It needed a phone in a hand for sixteen minutes.
findings.consequence: app-opened is the denominator of every funnel this channel exists to support, so completion rates read lower than they are.
findings.status: fixed; emitted from BorgarlandApplication.onCreate, which runs once per process, guarded by AppOpenedOncePerProcessTest

findings.what: The device fix supplies the coordinate, its accuracy is measured, and nothing gates or stores it. DeviceFix.liveFix races every enabled provider and takes whichever answers first; usable() checks only that the numbers are finite.
findings.evidence: Two fixes in one session, 14 m and 51 m, both resolving in about 240 ms, which is a network or cached fix rather than GPS. The 51 m one is the coordinate on the submitted report.
findings.consequence: The reports table has no accuracy column, so nothing downstream can tell a good fix from a poor one. The relay then appends a specific house number derived from it, and the address sentence is more precise than the coordinate that produced it.
findings.correctedInIssue: #31's body claimed DeviceFix already reasons about accuracy on the device path. It does not.

notFoundHere: Nothing about the city. The relay was unarmed, so the adapter, the city's validator and the reference-number parse were all untouched by this test (#56).
Nothing about a poor network. Both sends ran on wifi indoors; a 1390 ms send says little about the same walk on mobile data at the edge of coverage.
Nothing about the gallery path, which does not exist on either platform (#28). Every EXIF question this project has is a gallery-path question, and this test could not reach it.
Nothing about a cold outdoor GPS fix. Both fixes came from indoors in seconds, which is the case where the provider race resolves coarse.

tests.what: Verification of the #70 fix on the same phone that found it: the Activity destroyed and recreated three times inside one process, which is the exact condition that produced the duplicate.

build.hostVerifiedOn: the artifact: BorgarlandApplication is present in classes.dex, so Android had a class to instantiate

relay.note: Unarmed. No report was created; this test never left the camera screen.

tests.method: adb: force-stop for a fresh process, then launch, KEYCODE_BACK, launch, KEYCODE_BACK, launch, KEYCODE_HOME. Back finishes the Activity and clears the ViewModel while the process stays warm, which is what the first walk hit by hand. onStop flushes the buffer.

confirmed.claim: app-opened now fires once per process, whatever the Activity does.
confirmed.evidence: Three Activity creations in one session produced three camera-permission events and exactly one app-opened. The process id was unchanged throughout and the session id was unchanged, so this is one process.
confirmed.note: On the old code the same sequence would have produced three. The first walk produced two by accident; this produced one on purpose.

confirmed.claim: The manifest registration works, so the Application is actually instantiated.
confirmed.evidence: An app-opened event exists at all. An Application class Android is not told about is never constructed, and the event would simply have gone missing.

findings.what: camera-permission fires once per Activity creation, so it appeared three times in this session.
findings.whyNotADefect: It reports a state rather than a decision, and it is nobody's denominator: a session where the permission was granted is still countable as one. It is redundant rather than misleading, which is the difference from app-opened.

notFoundHere: Nothing about a rotation, which is the other way Android recreates an Activity. Back was used because it is scriptable over adb; the lifetime argument is the same either way.
Nothing about a process death and restore, where Android recreates the Activity after killing the process. That produces a NEW session, and a new app-opened is then correct.
Nothing about the rest of the walk. This session never captured a photo, so it says nothing about location, the category picker or a send.
